title: Epic Games Disney ortaklığı oyununu erteleyerek yapay zeka odaklı modele geçti
summary: Epic Games, Disney ortaklığıyla geliştirilen Marvel ve Star Wars karakterlerini içeren nişancı oyununu erteleyerek yapay zeka odaklı üretim modeline geçiş yaptı.
body:
Bloomberg'ün aktardığına göre Epic Games, Disney iş birliğiyle geliştirilen ve Marvel ile Star Wars karakterlerini barındıran yeni nişancı oyununun çıkışını erteledi. Normal şartlarda Mart ayında çıkması planlanan yapım için yeni bir takvim henüz açıklanmadı. Şirket içi bir toplantıda geliştiricilere, projede yapay zeka araçlarının kullanılacağı ve **yapay zeka** öncelikli bir sisteme geçileceği duyuruldu.

## Yapay zeka odaklı üretim süreci

Projede çalışan yönetmenlerden birinin mesajında el yazımı kod döneminin kapandığı ve oyun içerisindeki tüm görsellerin **tamamen yapay zeka** iş akışlarıyla üretileceği belirtildi. Geliştirme sürecinde Anthropic imzalı Claude gibi araçların kullanılacağı, insan çalışanların ise bu çıktıları denetleyeceği ifade edildi. Kararın açıklanmasının ardından bazı çalışanların şaşkınlık yaşadığı bildirildi.

## Epic Games'in stratejisi ve açıklamalar

Epic Games iletişim direktörü Jake Jones şirketin yapay zeka hızlandırmalı geliştirmeyi benimsediğini belirtti. Öte yandan CEO Tim Sweeney sosyal medya üzerinden yaptığı açıklamada, şirkette büyük bir dönüşüm yaşandığını ve amaçlarının daha az insanla aynı işi yapmak değil, ekiplerin daha fazla içerik üretmesini sağlamak olduğunu kaydetti.

**Neden önemli?** Oyun dünyasında tartışmalara yol açan yapay zeka kullanımı, büyük ölçekli bir yapım için ilk kez bu denli merkezi bir konuma getirilirken, projenin takviminde yaşanan gecikmeler de bu stratejik değişimin tetikleyicileri arasında yer aldı.

source_texts.title: Epic Games delays Disney game and tells developers to go "AI first"
source_texts.summary: Epic Games has delayed its upcoming Disney collaboration - a shooter featuring characters from the Marvel and Star Wars franchises - and told developers to move to an "AI first" production model. Read more
source_texts.text:
Epic Games has delayed its upcoming Disney collaboration - a shooter featuring characters from the Marvel and Star Wars franchises - and told developers to move to an "AI first" production model.

According to Bloomberg , the game had been slated for March, but no new release date has been confirmed.

People familiar with the project told the site that developers were asked to build the game with AI tools, including Anthropic's Claude, with staff overseeing the output.

In an internal message seen by Bloomberg, one of the game's directors told staff: "No more hand-written code." The director also said all of the game's art would be "generated with full AI workflows."

In a statement to Bloomberg, Epic communications director Jake Jones said the company is "embracing AI-accelerated development, led by Epic developers who are the visionaries and creative drivers for everything we do." Disney did not immediately respond to the outlet's request for comment.

Developers were told about the change on a video call last week, and some were "stunned" according to Bloomberg's sources.

The same sources also said development had fallen behind schedule, partly because Epic misjudged the staffing and time the game would need. Bloomberg noted that Epic was already encouraging AI use across its divisions, and said no other major games company has previously tried to make a game mostly with AI.

Disney invested $1.5 billion in Epic in 2024 and took an equity stake , and the two companies announced a partnership covering multiple games, with this shooter due to be the first. In March, Epic said it was cutting 1,000 jobs , in part due to slowing engagement in Fortnite.

A 2026 GDC survey found that more than a third of game developers use AI in their work , while more than half believe it is harmful to the industry.

Earlier today we reported that Yuji Horii, the creator of Dragon Quest, had produced a new game using AI in about 30 minutes .

Epic Games has reportedly instructed its developers to implement âAI-firstâ development and use âno more handwritten codeâ on an unannounced shooter.
Thatâs according to a report by Bloomberg, which claims that one of the unannounced gameâs directors told staff in an internal message that all art for the title would now be âgenerated with full AI workflows.â
The game in question is a collaboration with Disney â which invested $1.5 billion in Epic in 2024 â that is said to feature characters from both Marvel and Star Wars. Progress on the title has allegedly been slower than expected, partly because Epic underestimated how many staff it would require.
According to Bloomberg, developers were then told last week that the game would implement an âAI-firstâ production model using tools such as Anthropicâs Claude. Humans will then manage and guide that work, it’s claimed.
âThe announcement left some Epic developers stunned on a video call last week,â according to people who spoke to the publication. âSome made jokes about how they should handle errors produced by the AI-generated work, asking if they should ask Claude to fix its own mistakes.â
An Epic spokesperson said in a statement: “Weâre embracing AI-accelerated development, led by Epic developers who are the visionaries and creative drivers for everything we do.â
Adding further weight to the report,Â CEO Tim Sweeney wrote on social media on Monday: “We have a huge pivot underway here at Epic, moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration. The aim isn’t to do the same stuff with fewer people, but to enable everyone here to build MORE and BETTER stuff, and to bring the benefits to all teams using Unreal.”
The Fortnite maker has previously endorsed generative AI
The use of generative AI in game development remains a contentious issue, particularly because of concerns about plagiarism and the perceived poor quality of its results. However, many developers are pushing ahead, in an attempt to lower costs and speed up development.
Epic is one of the first major video-game companies to confirm that itâs attempting to build a triple-A game primarily with AI, but it’s previously backed the technology.
CEO Tim Sweeney has publicly endorsed the use of AI multiple times, stating that he believes it is âreally irresponsibleâ of Steam to make studios disclose AI use. In July, the executive implied that AI could âenableâ games like Sony and Bungieâs sunsetted live service shooter Destiny âto thriveâ.
In June 2026, it was announced that Epicâs Unreal Engine 6 will integrate AI tools to âgreatly reduce the tedious workâ in game development.
According to Epic, UE6 will introduce integrations with AI models such as Claude, Gemini, and others, which will act as âcreativity and productivity multipliers,â enabling teams to âfocus their efforts on the essential creative and technical tasks of development rather than time on time-consuming manual tasksâ.
